title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The previous and next pages in this folder are unrelated typescript (Dieudonné's Éléments n° 382, jets of sections), reused as scrap paper. This handwritten page is a computation in Dieudonné theory, presumably tied to the crystals / Barsotti–Tate material of 1970 (Montréal lectures).

Most plausible reading of the setting:
- K/Q_p is a finite extension with ring of integers O_K, ramification index e, residue degree f, and uniformizer π.
- G_0 is a p-divisible group over a perfect field k of characteristic p, with O_K-action, whose Dieudonné module M is free of rank 1 over O_K ⊗_{Z_p} W(k).
- After decomposing along the f embeddings of the maximal unramified subring W(F_{p^f}) (the f eigencomponents of W(F_{p^f}) ⊗ W(k)), M = ⊕_{ν∈Z/f} M_ν. Each M_ν is free of rank 1 over A = W(k)[π] (the symbol Ω on the page is probably the rank-one free module or basis on which the φ_ν act).
- Frobenius F_M is σ-semilinear and sends M_ν to M_{ν+1}. So it is given by f maps φ_ν, each a scalar in A.

The computation:
1. Choose bases so that φ_ν = π^{r_ν}·id for 0 ≤ ν ≤ f−2 (r_ν ≥ 0). The last map cannot be normalized as well: φ_{f−1} = λ·id with λ = π^{r_{f−1}} u, u ∈ A^*.
2. Then F_M^f, which is linear on each component, equals π^{r_0+…+r_{f−1}} u =: ϖ.
3. Condition (*)' is the existence of V with FV = VF = p. It says p is divisible by each φ_ν, i.e. 0 ≤ r_ν ≤ e for all ν.
4. M/F_M M ≅ A/uπ^{r_{f−1}}A ⊕ A/π^{r_0}A ⊕ … ⊕ A/π^{r_{f−2}}A. Its length (the length of A/ϖA) gives dim G_0 = Σ r_ν. This is ≤ fe = h, the height of G_0.
5. Conclusion: dim G_0 = 1 iff F_M^f is a uniformizer of A (one may take it to be π after changing π). Equivalently, exactly one r_{ν0} = 1, all others are 0, and u is a unit (u = 1 if ϖ = π).

This is the Dieudonné-module characterization of one-dimensional formal O_K-modules of height [K:Q_p] (Lubin–Tate type) among p-divisible groups with O_K-action of rank one. More generally, the tuple (r_ν) with 0 ≤ r_ν ≤ e classifies the invariants and gives the dimension.
errors: Minor: the normalization u = 1 needs a further change of basis (e.g. a Lang-type argument over algebraically closed or sufficiently large k). The page states it only parenthetically.
The page conflates 'F_M^f' and 'F_M' in the final equivalence. It should read: F_M^f is a uniformizer.
The setting (meaning of A, Ω, f, the condition (*)') is not fully specified on this page. The reading above is inferred.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard calculation: Dieudonné-module classification of rank-one O_K-modules and the characterization of the Lubin–Tate (dimension-1) case. It parallels Raynaud's later exponents 0 ≤ r_i ≤ e for F_q-vector space schemes, but nothing on the page appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Final equivalence should read 'F_M^f = ϖ_M est uniformisante de A', not 'F_M est uniformisante'.
'F_M f' in the displayed formula is F_M^f (f-th iterate).
The inserted marginal note near 'longueur' is likely 'long_A(A/ϖA)', i.e. the length of A/ϖA.
